title: HoloScript std host-ABI binding surface v0
boundary: Host functions the packaged @holoscript/std native traits reach through get_std_math_lib() / get_std_collections_lib(). Every call crosses the guest/host boundary as canonical strict JSON: arguments marshal guest-to-host as JSON values, results marshal host-to-guest as JSON values and are re-validated on re-entry (finite numbers, no negative zero, safe keys). All functions are pure and total over their documented domain; everything outside the domain is a structured fail-closed error, never a coercion, undefined, or NaN.

valueForms.number: finite IEEE-754 double, negative zero rejected
valueForms.list: JSON array; elements are any strict-JSON values under the same rails
valueForms.map: JSON object; string keys only; semantically unordered — key-order-observing operations return ascending key order
valueForms.set: JSON array in canonical set form: deduplicated and sorted ascending by the canonical JSON encoding of each element; set-typed inputs are re-canonicalized defensively
valueForms.quat: JSON object { x, y, z, w } of numbers
valueForms.equality: structural: two values are equal when their canonical JSON encodings are identical

referenceOracle: packages/std TypeScript twin (math.ts / collections.ts). The binding is twin-derived with fail-closed rails added; where the twin uses JS reference identity (indexOf/includes/Set dedupe) the ABI hardens to structural equality, so twin agreement is asserted only on vectors whose semantics coincide (scalar elements). Functions with twinRef null are binding-defined.

clamp.semantics: min <= result <= max via max(min, min(max, value))

quat_slerp.semantics: shortest-path spherical interpolation with nlerp fallback above dot 0.9995, mirroring the twin term order

list_of.semantics: identity over the already-JSON argument array

list_range.semantics: start inclusive, end exclusive, sign-aware like the twin loop; step 0 or step sign moving away from end is an error

list_repeat.semantics: count copies; count must be a non-negative integer

list_flatten.semantics: one level of nesting removed; non-array elements pass through

list_get.semantics: zero-based; index must be an integer within bounds

list_first.semantics: first element; empty list is an error

list_last.semantics: last element; empty list is an error

list_join.semantics: elements must be strings or numbers; anything else is an error (no implicit toString)

list_zip.semantics: pairs [a[i], b[i]] up to the shorter length

list_chunk.semantics: consecutive sublists of at most size; size must be a positive integer

map_get.semantics: value at key; absent key is an error (the twin returns undefined, which does not exist in strict JSON)

map_delete.semantics: copy without key; deleting an absent key is a no-op

map_entries.semantics: [key, value] pairs in ascending key order

map_merge.semantics: b wins on key collisions, like the twin

excludedHigherOrder.reason: list_map, list_flat_map, list_filter, list_reduce, list_sort(comparator), map_map_values, and map_filter take function-valued parameters; the deterministic subsets have no function values or closures
excludedHigherOrder.unlock: a bounded guest-callback design (host re-enters the guest evaluator per element) or declarative predicate/projection mini-expressions
